newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle trade light at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle trade light at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Wednesday traded at $70.00 per cwt near midday, unchanged from last week, feedlot sources said.
Up to 4,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and in Kansas, they said.
However, many feedlot operators resisted further bids at $70.00 amid ideas that fed cattle could trade at $71.00 or $72.00 because of tight finished cattle supplies, the feedlot sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices also were underpinned by gains in CME live cattle futures and outlooks for firm beef prices.
Beef demand from retailers for November promotions, ahead of seasonal ham and turkey features, kept product flowing, but packers were still discounting prices.
Beef prices were quoted down $0.54 to $0.94 per cwt, with 225 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Demand for finished cattle was strong because owners continue to pull cattle ahead to market them early while profits remain, market sources said.
Cattle owners on average were making about $85.00 per head at the $70.00 level, aided in part by lower feed costs now that new crop grains were being harvested, the sources said.
